title: High throughput HIV-1 microneutralization assay
protocol: Select two strains that are most potently neutralized by the donor’s serum or easy-to-neutralize strains such as HIV-1-BaL and HIV-1-MN.
Titer pseudovirus stock in a mock neutralization assay using medium as a substitute for antibody.
Prepare 11 2-fold serial dilutions of each virus.
Prepare 11 5-fold serial dilutions of each virus.
Include DEAE-dextran to facilitate viral entry if necessary.
Choose a dilution that gives a signal of 40,000 to 100,000 RLU, which is 50-100 fold above background.
Thaw supernatants and dilute virus in complete DMEM using the concentration titered in step 2.
Transfer 20 μl of virus to each of the 2 plates harvested at step 48.
Mix 20 μl of supernatant with each transferred virus on the plates.
Incubate at 37°C for 45-90 minutes.
Discard TZM-bl culture media during incubation.
Remove adherent cells by slowly adding 5 ml of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA.
Incubate at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Add 10 ml of complete DMEM and suspend the cells by gentle pipet action.
Transfer the suspension to a 50 ml conical tube.
Spin, resuspend in complete DMEM, and count the cells.
Dilute TZM-bl cells in complete DMEM to a concentration of 1.5 x 10^5.
Add DEAE–dextran at an optimized concentration of approximately 7.5 µg/ml.
Dispense cells to each well of the assay plate at a total of 3x10^3 cells per well.
Incubate for 48-54 hours at 37°C.
Remove 30 μl from each assay well.
Lyse the cells with the addition of 30 µl of Britelite Plus substrate.
Read in a luminometer capable of accurately reading 384-well plates.
Subtract the average signal from cells-only wells from all wells.
Average the signal from wells with feeders but no B cells.
Calculate % neutralization using the formula: (Vo - Vn) / Vo * 100, where Vn is the RLU in virus plus antibody wells and Vo is the RLU in virus only wells.
